# local 0017: mcs51: a C23 function declared (...) reads wrong arguments, and its result in A is lost after a call with more than 3 bytes of arguments

- Category: [Problems without a ticket and without a patch](../../unreported.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17228
- Recommended action: Set FUNC_HASSTACKPARM in processFuncArgs() for a reentrant function declared (...). Make vaargs-c23 execute its assertions.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17228, the program below stores `01 00` at xdata 0x7000 in uCsim, and `02 07` is correct. The
command is `sdcc -mmcs51 --std-c23 va.c`. `--model-large` gives the same bytes with and without
`--std-c23`. Without it, sdcc gives warning 350 for each function declared `(...)`.

```c
#include <stdarg.h>

__xdata __at (0x7000) volatile unsigned char result[2];

unsigned char zero (...) { return 0; }
unsigned char test (void) { if (zero (1, 2)) return 1; return 2; }

unsigned char
first (...)
{
  va_list ap;
  unsigned char x;

  va_start (ap);
  x = va_arg (ap, int);
  va_end (ap);
  return x;
}

void main (void) { result[0] = test (); result[1] = first (7); for (;;); }
```

- The calling code. `test()` has `lcall _zero`, `mov a,sp`, `add a,#0xfc`, `mov sp,a`, `jz`, so the
  jump tests the stack pointer. `zero (1, 2) | g` is also wrong. `zero (1, 2) + 0x40`, an
  assignment of the result to a local, and a call with 2 bytes of arguments are correct. With the
  fork's patch for bug #4253, `push acc` and `pop acc` enclose the three instructions, `pop acc`
  reads an argument byte, and `test()` also returns 1.
- The called function. `first()` begins with `mov a,bp`, `add a,#0xfd`, and it does not have
  `push bp`, `mov bp,sp`. A function declared `(...)` that has an array on the stack sets `bp` and
  returns its argument.

A function with a named parameter before `...` is correct in both places. Each place was also run
in a program of its own with `--model-large --stack-auto`, with the same faults.

## Cause

`processFuncArgs()` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` sets `FUNC_HASSTACKPARM` inside its loop over the named
parameters. A function declared `(...)` does not have one, so the flag is 0, and all its arguments
are on the stack. `packRegsForAccUse()` in `src/mcs51/ralloc.c` keeps the result of a call out of
A only for a reentrant function with the flag, and `genCall()` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` uses A to
remove more than 3 bytes of arguments. `genFunction()` emits `push bp`, `mov bp,sp` only for
`sym->stack || FUNC_HASSTACKPARM (ftype)`, and the code addresses `__va_start` through `bp`. The
rule for `(...)` in `src/SDCC.y` is from [r15891](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/15891/), the
merge of the branch `arraybounds`. A patch is not offered. `ds390` and `pic16` also test the flag,
and they were not compiled.

## Related

- `support/regression/tests/vaargs-c23.c.in` has functions of this form. On r17228 it reports 0
  tests for host, stm8, ucz80, and the mcs51 targets small, medium, large, huge, small-stack-auto,
  and large-stack-auto. With `sdcc -mmcs51`, its `#if (__STDC_VERSION_STDARG_H__ >= 202311L)` is
  false, because `#pragma std_c23` does not change `__STDC_VERSION__` in the preprocessor, which
  is 201112L without `--std-c23`.
